q: 1. The loss of head due to sudden enlargement is
explain: This loss represents energy dissipated through turbulence as flow transitions to a larger pipe.

q: 2. The loss of head due to sudden contraction, assuming coefficient of contraction as 0.62, is
explain: Based on (1/Cc - 1)² * (v₂²/2g). With Cc = 0.62, the factor is approx 0.375.

q: 3. The loss of head at entrance in a pipe is
explain: Standard minor loss coefficient for a sharp-edged entrance is K = 0.5.

q: 4. The loss of head at exit of a pipe is
explain: At the exit, the entire kinetic energy (v²/2g) is lost as the fluid enters the reservoir.

q: 5. According to Darcy's formula, the loss of head due to friction in the pipe is ............
explain: The standard Darcy-Weisbach equation is often expressed as $h_f =  rac{4flv^2}{2gd}$ where $f$ is the friction factor.

q: 6. The hydraulic mean depth or the hydraulic radius is the ratio of ............
options: area of flow and wetted perimeter
wetted perimeter and diameter of pipe
velocity of flow and area of flow
explain: Hydraulic mean depth ($m$ or $R$) is defined as the cross-sectional area of flow ($A$) divided by the wetted perimeter ($P$).

q: 7. The hydraulic mean depth for a circular pipe of diameter (d) is ............
explain: For a full pipe: $A =  rac{\pi d^2}{4}$ and $P = \pi d$. Thus, $m = A/P = ( rac{\pi d^2}{4}) / \pi d = d/4$.

q: 8. The efficiency of power transmission through pipe is ............
explain: Efficiency is the ratio of available head at the outlet ($H - h_f$) to the total head supplied at the inlet ($H$).

q: 9. The power transmitted through a pipe is ............
explain: Power is given by $P = \gamma Q H_{net}$, where $H_{net}$ is the total head minus friction losses ($H - h_f$).

q: 10. The power transmitted through the pipe is maximum when the head lost due to friction is equal to ............
options: one-fourth of the total supply head
one-third of the total supply head
one-half of the total supply head
two-third of the total supply head
explain: By differentiating the power equation with respect to velocity, we find that maximum power occurs when $h_f = H/3$.

q: 11. The maximum efficiency of transmission through a pipe is ............
explain: At maximum power transmission ($h_f = H/3$), efficiency $\eta = (H - H/3) / H = 2/3$, which is 66.67%.

q: 12. A compound pipe is required to be replaced by a new pipe. The two pipes are said to be equivalent, if ............
options: length of both the pipes is same
diameter of both the pipes is same
loss of head and discharge of both the pipes is same
loss of head and velocity of flow in both the pipes is same
explain: An equivalent pipe must carry the same discharge ($Q$) with the same total head loss ($h_f$) as the original system of pipes.

q: 13. A compound pipe of diameter d1, d2 and d3 having lengths l1, l2 and l3 is to be replaced by an equivalent pipe of uniform diameter d and of the same length (l) as that of the compound pipe. The size of the equivalent pipe is given by ............
explain: This is known as Dupuit’s equation: $ rac{l}{d^5} = \sum  rac{l_i}{d_i^5}$, derived from equating friction losses.

q: 14. An air vessel is provided at the summit in a siphon to ............
explain: Air vessels at the summit collect air that comes out of solution at low pressure, preventing an air lock which would interrupt the siphonic action.

q: 15. A nozzle is generally made of ............
explain: Nozzles are designed to increase the velocity of fluid at the expense of pressure; a convergent shape achieves this for incompressible fluids.

q: 16. A nozzle placed at the end of a water pipe line discharges water at a ............
explain: The primary function of a nozzle is to convert pressure energy into kinetic energy, resulting in a high-velocity jet.

q: 17. The power transmitted through the nozzle is maximum when the head lost due to friction in the pipe is ............ of the total supply head.
explain: Similar to pipe transmission, the maximum power through a nozzle is achieved when head loss $h_f = H/3$.

q: 18. The diameter of the nozzle (d) for maximum transmission of power is given by ............
explain: For maximum power, the optimal nozzle diameter is $d = ( rac{D^5}{8fl})^{1/4}$.

q: 19. The hammer blow in pipes occurs when ............
options: there is excessive leakage in the pipe
the pipe bursts under high pressure of fluid
the flow of fluid through the pipe is suddenly brought to rest by closing of the valve
the flow of fluid through the pipe is gradually brought to rest by closing of the valve
explain: Water hammer (hammer blow) is a pressure surge caused when a fluid in motion is forced to stop or change direction suddenly.

q: 20. A channel is said to be of most economical cross-section, if ............
options: it gives maximum discharge for a given cross-section
it involves lesser excavation for the designed amount of discharge
explain: The most economical section (or most efficient section) is designed to minimize the wetted perimeter for a given area, which maximizes discharge and minimizes excavation costs.

q: 21. The discharge through a channel of circular section will be maximum when the depth of water is ............ the diameter of the circular channel.
explain: While velocity is maximum at 0.81d, the maximum discharge in a circular channel occurs when the depth $y = 0.95d$ due to the large increase in area.

q: 22. The velocity through a channel of circular section will be maximum when the depth of water is ............ the diameter of the circular channel.
explain: Maximum velocity in a circular pipe occurs when the depth of flow is 0.81 times the diameter.

q: 23. The highest efficiency is obtained with a channel of ............ section.
explain: Among the common polygonal shapes, the trapezoidal section (specifically a half-hexagon) is the most efficient open channel section.

q: 24. In open channels, the specific energy is the ............
options: total energy measured with respect to the datum passing through the bottom of the channel
total energy measured above the horizontal datum
kinetic energy plotted above the free surface of water
explain: Specific energy ($E$) is the energy of flow per unit weight of water measured with the channel bed as the datum: $E = y + v^2/2g$.

q: 25. The critical depth for a channel is given by ............
explain: For a rectangular channel, the critical depth ($y_c$) is calculated as $\sqrt[3]{q^2/g}$, where $q$ is the discharge per unit width.

q: 26. If the depth of water in an open channel is greater than the critical depth, the flow is called ............
explain: When $y > y_c$, the velocity is low and the flow is described as tranquil, subcritical, or streaming flow.

q: 27. If the depth of water in an open channel is less than the critical depth, the flow is called ............
explain: When $y < y_c$, the velocity is high and the flow is described as torrential, supercritical, or shooting flow.

q: 28. The most efficient section of a channel is ............
explain: The trapezoidal section is generally considered the most efficient because it can most closely approximate a semi-circle, which has the minimum wetted perimeter.

q: 29. The critical depth meter is used to measure ............
options: velocity of flow in an open channel
depth of flow in an open channel
explain: A critical depth meter is a device used in open channels to measure the depth of flow by creating a critical flow condition.

q: 30. The flow in a pipe is turbulent when Reynold number is ............
explain: In pipe flow, $Re > 2800$ (or often cited as 4000 in some texts) is generally considered turbulent.

q: 31. The flow in a pipe is neither laminar nor turbulent when Reynold number is ............
explain: This range is known as the 'transition zone' where the flow is unstable.

q: 32. The loss of head due to viscosity for laminar flow in pipes is ............
explain: From the Hagen-Poiseuille equation, $h_f = 32 \mu v L / \gamma D^2$.

q: 33. The loss of head due to friction in a pipe of uniform diameter in which a viscous flow is taking place, is ............... where, Rn = Reynold number
explain: For laminar (viscous) flow in a pipe, the friction factor 'f' is given by 64/Re. Therefore, the head loss is directly related to this coefficient.

q: 34. Frictional loss of head includes the loss of energy due to ...............
explain: Head loss occurs due to internal friction between fluid layers (viscosity) and mixing/eddies in the flow (turbulence).

q: 35. Hydraulic grade line ...............
options: remains above the centre line of conduit
remains below the centre line of conduit
remains parallel to the centre line of conduit
may be above or below the centre line of conduit
explain: While usually above the conduit, the HGL can fall below the pipe centerline if there is negative (vacuum) pressure in the system.

q: 36. If the total head of the nozzle of a pipe is 37.5 m and discharge is 1 cumec, the power generated is ...............
explain: Power (P) = (wQH)/75 in metric HP. (1000 * 1 * 37.5) / 75 = 500 H.P.

q: 37. The ratio of frictional factor and coefficient of friction used in general equation for a equation for a head loss in a pipe, is ...............
explain: Friction factor (f) is typically defined as 4 times the coefficient of friction (f'). f = 4f'.

q: 38. Manning's formula is used for ...............
options: head loss due to friction in open channels
head loss due to friction in pipes flowing full
explain: Manning's formula ($V =  rac{1}{n} R^{2/3} S^{1/2}$) is the most widely used empirical formula for uniform flow in open channels.

q: 39. In an inclined pipe, the pressure differentiate its two ends is due to ...............
explain: While gravity affects the pressure at different elevations, the continuous pressure 'differentiation' or loss as fluid flows between two points in a pipe is primarily caused by friction against the pipe walls.

q: 40. A siphon is used ...............
options: to connect water reservoirs at different levels intervened by a hill
to supply water to town from higher level to lower level
to fill up a tank with water at higher level from a lower level
explain: A siphon is a long bent pipe used to carry water from a higher reservoir to a lower reservoir when the two are separated by a high ridge or hill.

q: 41. To avoid an interruption in the flow of a siphon, a vessel is provided ...............
options: at any point between inlet and outlet
explain: An air vessel is provided at the summit to collect any air that comes out of solution due to low pressure, preventing an air lock that would stop the flow.

q: 42. For a long pipe, the head loss ...............
options: at the entrance and outlet both are ignored
explain: In 'long pipes' (usually where $L > 1000D$), minor losses like entrance and exit losses are negligible compared to the major loss caused by friction.

q: 43. To replace a pipe of diameter D by n parallel pipes of diameter d, the formula is ...............
explain: Equating the discharges and using Darcy's equation for both cases results in the relation $D^5 = n^2 \cdot d^5$, which simplifies to $d = D / n^{2/5}$.

q: 44. For solving network problems of pipes, necessary condition is ...............
explain: Solving pipe networks (like Hardy Cross method) requires satisfying flow continuity at junctions, energy conservation in loops, and using head loss formulas like Darcy-Weisbach.

q: 45. Power transmitted through a pipe is maximum when friction head loss, is ...............
options: one-half of the total head supplied
one-third of the total head supplied
one-fourth of the total head supplied
equal to the total head supplied
explain: The condition for maximum power transmission efficiency occurs when the head lost due to friction ($h_f$) is equal to $H/3$, where $H$ is the total head.

q: 46. Maximum efficiency of transmission of power through a pipe, is ...............
explain: Efficiency is given by $(H - h_f)/H$. Substituting the maximum power condition ($h_f = H/3$), we get $(H - H/3)/H = 2/3$, which is approximately 66.67%.

q: 47. For maximum horse power of a nozzle, the head supplied must be equal to ...............
options: head loss in the pipe due to friction
twice the head loss in the pipe due to friction
thrice the head loss in the pipe due to friction
four times the head loss in the pipe due to friction
explain: Similar to power transmission in pipes, the power at the nozzle is maximum when the friction head loss is one-third of the total head, meaning $H = 3h_f$.

q: 48. Hydraulic gradient is equal ...............
options: difference in water surfaces / total length of the channel
head loss due to friction / total length of the channel
wetted perimeter / total length of the channel
area of the cross-section / total length of the channel
explain: The Hydraulic Gradient Line (HGL) represents the slope of the piezometric head, calculated as the head loss per unit length of the pipe or channel ($h_f/L$).

q: 49. The ratio of the hydraulic radius of a pipe running full to the hydraulic radius of a square section of a channel whose side is equal to the diameter of the pipe, is ...............
explain: Hydraulic radius of pipe ($D/4$) and square ($a^2/4a = a/4$). Since side $a = D$, the ratio is $(D/4) / (D/4) = 1$.

q: 50. Hydraulic radius is equal to ...............
options: area divided by square of wetted perimeter
explain: The hydraulic radius (R or m) is a measure of channel efficiency, defined as the ratio of the cross-sectional area (A) to the wetted perimeter (P): $R = A/P$.
